title: Spinach and Ricotta Lasagne
changes_from_base: Meat ragù replaced by wilted, well-drained spinach folded into seasoned ricotta with egg and Parmesan; mozzarella between the layers.
summary: This follows the classic lasagne bolognese method, but swaps the meat ragù for wilted, well-drained spinach folded into seasoned ricotta with egg and Parmesan, layered with mozzarella and béchamel.
equipment: food processor or large bowl and whisk

ingredients.item: fresh spinach, washed (or 600 g frozen leaf spinach, thawed)
fine sea salt or table salt
Parmesan or a vegetarian hard cheese, finely grated

steps.title: Wilt the spinach
steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat and soften the shallot and garlic for 1 minute. Add the spinach in handfuls, stirring each batch down before adding the next, until fully wilted. Keep cooking until the liquid it releases has evaporated and the pan looks dry, since watery spinach is the most common cause of a soggy lasagne.

steps.title: Drain and chop
steps.text: Tip the wilted spinach into a fine sieve and press down hard with a spatula to squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Roughly chop the drained spinach. The drier it is now, the firmer each slice of lasagne will hold together later.

steps.title: Mix the ricotta filling
steps.text: Blend or whisk the ricotta, egg, Parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper together until smooth. Fold in the drained, chopped spinach until evenly distributed through the mixture. The egg sets lightly as the lasagne bakes, holding the ricotta in soft, sliceable layers rather than letting it ooze out.

steps.title: Make the béchamel
steps.text: Melt the butter in a medium saucepan, then whisk in the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes without letting it colour, to cook out the raw flour taste. Gradually whisk in the warm milk, a little at a time, keeping the sauce smooth before each new addition. Add the bay leaf and salt and simmer for 8-10 minutes, whisking often, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon; discard the bay leaf once done.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, so the dish cooks evenly from the moment it goes in. Use this time to have the baking dish, lasagne sheets and remaining ingredients ready for assembly.

steps.title: Layer the lasagne
steps.text: Spread a thin coat of béchamel over the base of the 23 x 33 cm dish, then add a layer of sheets, a third of the spinach-ricotta mixture, a little béchamel and a quarter of the mozzarella. Repeat this layering twice more, then finish with a final layer of sheets, the rest of the béchamel, and the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan on top. Make sure every sheet touches sauce, as any dry patch of pasta will stay hard and chalky once baked.

steps.title: Bake covered then open
steps.text: Cover the dish loosely with tented foil, so it doesn't touch the cheese, and bake on the tray for 30 minutes. Uncover and bake for a further 20-25 minutes, until the top is bubbling and golden and a knife slides through the layers easily; check the centre reaches 74°C. The uncovered stage lets the top brown and crisp while the inside finishes cooking through.

steps.title: Rest before serving
steps.text: Leave the lasagne to rest for 15 minutes before cutting. This short rest lets the béchamel and ricotta layers firm up slightly, so slices lift out cleanly instead of collapsing.

tips: Squeeze the spinach as dry as possible - leftover water is the main reason spinach lasagne turns watery.
Make sure every pasta sheet is covered in sauce; dry edges stay hard and crunchy after baking.
Let the lasagne rest for the full 15 minutes before slicing, or the layers will slide apart.
Check the centre reaches 74°C before serving, especially if your oven runs cool.
storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate covered for up to 3 days or freeze (baked or unbaked) for up to 3 months. Reheat in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven, covered, until piping hot and the centre reaches 74°C. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
